subject: DPA onboarding checklist & locality sprint — timeline and evidence cadence
messages:
From: Emma Tang <emma.tang@healthly.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Andrew Cole <andrew.cole@procurecorp.com>
Date: Sat, 1 Aug 2026 16:15:00 +0200
Subject: DPA onboarding questions + locality constraints (initial)

Hi Mina / Kimberly,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. We're excited about Redwood but need to align on two things before legal will sign the DPA: 1) a clear acceptance checklist for region-constrained processing (EU-only for Healthly EHR data, with a documented temporary failover window), and 2) the set of subprocessors that will have access to telemetry/audit logs for the EU tenant.

Can you share a short onboarding checklist that outlines what evidence we will receive (subprocessor roster, KMS key custody, audit-log samples, and deployment topology), and a proposed sprint timeline for delivering those artifacts? We also need the list of evidence types in order of priority so our security team can run a gap analysis.

I've attached our DPA questionnaire (Healthly_DPA_Questionnaire_v2.xlsx) — it contains some follow-ups in the last tab. If possible, include an expected date for when Redwood can provide:
- Subprocessor roster with activation dates
- Evidence of EU-only placement for custody-sensitive flows
- Audit-log sample (redacted) showing regional ingress/egress

Looking for a readiness window of ~4 weeks but open to your proposal. If you have an intake checklist + one-page sprint plan, that will help accelerate our internal sign-off.

Best,
Emma
Security & Privacy, Healthly

Attachments: Healthly_DPA_Questionnaire_v2.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Tang <emma.tang@healthly.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 1 Aug 2026 12:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DPA onboarding questions + locality constraints (initial)

Hi Emma — thanks for sending the questionnaire and the clear asks.

Summary / proposed plan (high level):
1) Intake checklist (we'll deliver within 3 business days):
   - Completed subprocessor roster (current + 30d activation window)
   - KMS approach doc (customer-managed KMS options + split-key/escrow notes)
   - Short deployment topology (how we guarantee EU placement and where transient hops may occur)
2) Evidence sprint (target 3-week sprint after checklist sign-off):
   - Week 1: Subprocessor roster + KMS proof-of-concept (screenshots/config snippets)
   - Week 2: Audit-log sample (redacted) and placement verification artifacts (telemetry maps)
   - Week 3: Ops-runbook for temporary failover (ephemeral hop <= 72h) and handoff items for your security team
3) Acceptance criteria (we will draft and include these in the checklist):
   - Subprocessor roster delivered + attestation of no new EU-exposed subprocessors in the 30d window
   - KMS ownership options documented; if Healthly elects customer-managed keys, we will provide integration steps
   - Audit-log sample demonstrates EU ingress and indicates no persistent cross-border egress for covered flows

Attachments: a preliminary sprint plan (redwood-locality-sprint-plan.pdf) and an ops-runbook stub that details the ephemeral-failover play. I'll route the final checklist to you after internal sign-off from Tech Ops (cc'd Vivek for scheduling).

Link to evidence folder (we'll populate): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2B3cD_redwood-evidence

If that timeline works, can you confirm Healthly's prioritized evidence list (from your side) and a preferred SLA for the acceptance review (e.g., 5 business days to review each artifact)?

Thanks — Mina
Senior Privacy & Compliance, Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-locality-sprint-plan.pdf (one-pager), ops-runbook-temporary-egress.md (text)

Subject: Re: DPA onboarding questions + locality constraints (technical notes)

Emma / Mina — adding a few ops-level clarifications that will affect what we deliver as "evidence" and the sprint scope.

Operational notes:
- Placement guarantee: we operate region affinity with pinned placements for customer tenants. For EU-only custody flows we use strict placement policies for model execution and persistent storage. However, ephemeral KV cache replication for cold-warm node warming may touch a cross-region hop in rare burst conditions — we log and surface those events.
- Temporary failover/fallback: our standard approach is an ephemeral hop (documented) of up to 72 hours for emergency failover. We capture telemetry and flag to the tenant; that event will create a time-bound incident report.
- Audit logs: we can provide a redacted audit sample that includes timestamps, region identifiers, and the affected request hashes — we'll scrub PII per your guidance.

I've attached an ops runbook excerpt (ops-runbook-temporary-egress.md) that shows the incident lifecycle and evidence artifacts we generate (playbook + logs + post-failover attestation). Also filed a tech ticket to track delivery: INFRA-7891 (https://jira.redwood.ai/browse/INFRA-7891).

Mina — once Healthly confirms prioritization and review SLAs, I'll calendar the work with the SRE squad.

—Kim
Engineering Manager, Reliability

Attachments: ops-runbook-temporary-egress.md (runbook excerpt)

Mina / team — quick executive note. This looks like the right approach: deliver the intake checklist quickly and prioritize the subprocessor roster + audit-log sample in week 1. Two asks from me:

1) Include a short acceptance-and-escalation paragraph in the checklist so Legal at Healthly knows who to contact if an artifact is not accepted within the SLA window.
2) Please add a single-line bullet on cost/contract impacts for customer-managed KMS vs Redwood-managed keys (high-level estimate only).

Mina — please send the checklist and sprint one-pager to Healthly and include Legal (legal@healthly.com) in the next update. I want a copy in the evidence Drive folder and the JIRA ticket referenced. Target: checklist out by Tue 2026-08-04 EOD.

Thanks — Laura
